issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'אִישׁ מֵאֵת מַכָּרוֹ' means 'each man from his acquaintance' (i.e., each priest from his own donor/acquaintance), but the Vietnamese 'từ những người quen biết mình' ('from those who know him') loses the distributive 'each man' (אִישׁ) and the singular 'his acquaintance' (מַכָּרוֹ), making it a general statement rather than each priest receiving from his own acquaintance. This changes the meaning slightly.

The Hebrew 'לְכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִמָּצֵא שָׁם בָּדֶק' means 'for all/wherever a breach is found there' — the Vietnamese renders 'wherever any damage may be found' which is acceptable, but the word 'there' (שָׁם) is omitted, though this is minor and does not change the meaning.
